findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has wrong substring index and inverted check
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at characters 4-6 of the prefix (substring(4,6)), but the matcher reads substring(3,5). It also returns false when the values are equal, which inverts the check. A wrong grant type passes as long as the UUID part is valid, so the matcher never verifies the grant and these integration assertions cannot catch encoding regressions. Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

findings.title: rawTokenId null check validates grantType instead
findings.body: The fourth `requireNonNull` passes `grantType` with the message for rawTokenId, so a null `rawTokenId` is accepted silently. Tokens could then be encoded with the literal suffix "null".

findings.title: Token creation fails for grant types that are not registered OAuth2GrantType providers
findings.body: `initToken` always calls `encodeTokenId`, which throws IllegalStateException when the grant type has no registered OAuth2GrantType factory. One example is the pre-authorized code grant when OID4VC_VCI is disabled. Another is any custom code path that sets an unregistered string in `Constants.GRANT_TYPE`. Token issuance would then fail with a 500 error. The legacy TokenExchangeProvider path also never sets GRANT_TYPE, so it falls back to "na" and silently loses the grant information.

findings.title: Duplicate shortcut detection via map sizes is unreliable
findings.body: If two grants share a shortcut, grantsByShortcuts has one fewer entry than grantsToShortcuts, so that case is detected. A custom grant whose shortcut is "na" collides with the UNKNOWN entry. Both maps can also shrink by the same amount in other collision cases. Separately, OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() is a new abstract method, which breaks third-party grant factories at compile time or with AbstractMethodError. It also has no length validation, while the decoder assumes exactly 2 characters. Consider a default implementation plus explicit validation.
